keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Schwerin row). The page gives no area or town list; a 25 km radius at Schwerin (gazetteer: 2,023 km2) is a soft stand-in.

ledger.note: 1161: the county. The lead: 'a county in the Mecklenburg region of the Holy Roman Empire that was created in 1161'; 'Gunzelin I was first mentioned as count of Schwerin one year later, in 1161' and 'In 1160, Henry the Lion defeated Niklot and conquered the Slavic castle in Schwerin.' The page names no land beyond Schwerin.

7 December 1368: Plüschow. 'The County was bought by Albrecht II of Mecklenburg in the Treaty of Plüschow (7 December 1368)' (infobox: 'Schwerin was united into Mecklenburg by Henry IV: 1368'; the body adds 'The lands of the county were (re-)united into the Duchy of Mecklenburg in 1471'). The Mecklenburg dossier dates the same acquisition 1358.

certainty.note: The page gives neither an area nor a town list; the circle is a stand-in.

sources.title: County of Schwerin
sources.note: Created 1161; Gunzelin I first mentioned 1161; Henry the Lion took Schwerin 1160; bought by Albrecht II of Mecklenburg, Treaty of Pluschow 7 December 1368; united into Mecklenburg 1471.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Schwerin row; the Mecklenburg dossier names county-of-schwerin as the counterpart of its 1358 gain.

CONFLICT. This page ends the county in 1368 (infobox; the Treaty of Pluschow on 7 December 1368); the page behind the Mecklenburg dossier says Albrecht 'acquired the former County of Schwerin in 1358'. Both are kept as each page gives them. The infobox also names 'Henry IV' where the body names Albrecht II. The 1471 date is the reunion of the lands of the county into the duchy, after the state.

SHAPES. Place circle Schwerin, 25 km (the gazetteer resolves Schwerin). Page silent on area, towns and on Pribislav's mainland ('Henry returned the other conquered lands to Nikolot's son, Pribislav', no year).

NOT SETTLED. (1) No area or town list; (2) the 1358 against 1368 sale; (3) no vassalage or wars on the page.
